body:
@woodruffw (as requested after a private report to security@astral.sh)

## Summary

`uv auth login` stores credentials in a plaintext file whose permissions come from the process umask instead of being restricted to the owner. With the common umask `022`, other local users can read the stored token if they can traverse the user's home directory.

## Reproduction

uv 0.12.21, Linux, no keyring/native-auth:

```console
T=$(mktemp -d)
(umask 022; XDG_DATA_HOME=$T uv auth login --token dummy-token https://example.invalid/simple)
find $T -printf '%m %p\n'
```

Result:

```text
755 $T/uv/credentials
644 $T/uv/credentials/credentials.toml
666 $T/uv/credentials/credentials.toml.lock
```

## Cause

`TextCredentialStore::write` in `crates/uv-auth/src/store.rs` calls `fs::create_dir_all(...)` and `fs::write(path, content)` without setting a mode or calling `set_permissions`. It also carries an existing TODO about using an atomic write.

## Expected

- Directory `0700` and file `0600`, created with those modes from the start (for example via `OpenOptions::mode(0o600)` plus a temp-file-and-rename write).
- The lock file should not be `0666` either.
- Existing files and directories could be tightened on the next write.

`ssh`, `gh` and the AWS CLI behave this way.

## Impact

Low severity (requires a local attacker), but it is still credential disclosure: if the home directory is `0755` (common on older Debian/Ubuntu and many shared servers), any local user can read tokens for private indexes. Users currently have to work around it with `umask 077` or `chmod`.

Happy to test a fix.
title: uv auth login: credentials file and directory permissions follow umask instead of being owner-only
